title: Rollout can leave registrations on its previous host or key
description: Found during the workspace ownership audit. Rollout.qml:493-575 synchronizes and destroys using only its current host and rolloutId. The writable identity fields have no previous-owner unregister handoff. A living instance changing host or key can leave old paint and input registrations behind. This is a source-confirmed lifecycle omission with production reachability unverified, not the desktop fullscreen cause. Acceptance: settle whether host/key are lifetime-constant or support transfer; the stated contract then prevents orphaned registrations. Any requested verification must exercise real owner transfer and removal, not static source assertions.

title: Review and redesign every shell component with UIX before desktop integration
description:
The owner wants the complete qsm-shell component library reviewed against the installed qsm-uix guidance before redesigning the desktop. Every component needs a deliberate task, controls, interaction contract, visual hierarchy and motion, not merely a working story. Full redesign is permitted, including changing the shared silhouette. The complete audit precedes component repairs, which proceed one item at a time with owner acceptance. Desktop integration follows the accepted library.

## Before and after

| Input | Current evidence | Required result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose a library type | A component record and story may expose only some states and routes | One record covers the intended task, supported controls/states, current evidence, proposed design and explicit gaps |
| Inspect an interaction | A semantic action may run without proving pointer delivery | Real Qt-local input, component signals and resulting state are distinguished from setup and direct action calls |
| Capture a changed state | Static story capture starts a separate scene and can omit glyphs | Capture the selected running session and correlate identity, state, geometry, rendered output and errors |
| Approach a target | No per-type pointer acquisition or corridor account | Record actual hit geometry, approach assumptions, target difficulty, tolerance and interference with neighbours |

## Done when

- The catalog and exported types are reconciled. Every library type has an audit row and an existing or newly justified component record, including types not currently used by the desktop. Aliased story keys do not inflate coverage.
- Each record describes purpose and consequences, public actions, expected settings, supported states, pointer/keyboard/wheel/focus/accessibility routes, sizes, empty/long content, failure and cancellation, visual tokens, palette roles and motion. Proposed capability is distinct from current implementation.
- Each interactive target has rendered and hit geometry in logical coordinates, relevant screen scale, clipping/visibility/occlusion facts, representative starting positions, approach distance and width, tolerance, neighbour interference and trigger-to-popup paths where applicable. Non-interactive types explicitly say not applicable. Modelled trajectories are not called measured human averages.
- Each record separates source-reviewed, runtime-exercised and owner-accepted. Runtime findings cite the exercised state and artefact. Unsupported/offscreen-only routes remain not tested, never pass. No blank capture or direct action call is accepted as proof of a visible control or native input.
- Workbench changes are restricted to capture and input blockers encountered by this audit. Prefer headless and Qt-local input without compuse or OS cursor movement. Isolated visible windows on workspace 10 are available when offscreen evidence is insufficient. No production restart or real-service mutation is implied.
- Findings distinguish source-backed defects, redesign choices, source conflicts and hypotheses. A shared design source resolves UIX conflicts before component repairs. No arbitrary palette or geometry threshold is labelled an external standard.
- After the complete audit, repair one component at a time and obtain owner acceptance before proceeding. The owner may change visual identity and silhouette. Desktop integration is a later phase after the library, not parallel implementation.

## Boundaries

No skill evals, unbounded review loops, Workbench chrome redesign, production hardware actions, user pointer telemetry or automatic acceptance. Preserve existing dirty Workbench work. Do not create speculative controls merely to collect features. Store per-element contracts and findings in docs/components/<Type>.md, with the catalog index and shared method linked rather than duplicated in README.

## Pointer model

Use actual rendered/input geometry, not icon size. Compare target acquisition with the Shannon difficulty ID = log2(1 + D/W) in bits, stating the selected 2D width model and approach direction. Do not predict milliseconds without calibrated movement data. Rectangular centre-line approach width and smaller-of-width/height are alternative models, not interchangeable physical measurements. Keep hover corridor continuity and timing as separate checks from target acquisition.

Primary source: MacKenzie and Buxton, Extending Fitts' Law to Two-Dimensional Tasks, CHI 1992, https://www.yorku.ca/mack/CHI92.html. Its regression coefficients are not the owner's mouse calibration. The current owner additionally requires hitbox mathematics and records per component.

## Ownership

qsm-shell owns reusable components, provider fixtures and per-type records. qsm-workbench owns session capture and native driver mechanics. qsm-desktop owns production services, composition, masks, monitors and policy. The marketplace task qsm-d0c.5 records the real-use trial of the UIX guidance, not acceptance of the entire redesign.

title: Audit every shell type and record behavior, UIX findings and hitbox math
description:
## Why

The owner needs a complete UIX review before accepting component repairs or desktop integration.
Existing stories and short records do not establish input reachability, visual polish or forgiving
hit geometry across the library.

## What Changes

- Reconcile exported types, story aliases, component records and current desktop use.
- Extend `docs/components/<Type>.md` with intended behavior, current evidence and redesign findings.
- Add per-target hitbox and pointer-path mathematics, explicitly separating models from user data.
- Keep one shared audit method and coverage index in `docs/USAGE.md`.
- Use the installed Workbench for requested isolated runtime evidence. Missing capture/input
  capability is a named gap, not a pass.
- Complete the full audit before component repairs. Redesign, including the silhouette, is
  permitted but is not implemented by this audit change.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `component-audit`: complete, source-linked per-component design and evidence contracts.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

`docs/components/*.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, and open findings in `docs/BACKLOG.md`.
No production component, theme, shader, service or compositor change. No dependency installation.
Workbench session capture is owned by its separate `session-render-capture` change.

## Critiques

- Devil's advocate: a generic checklist could impersonate a real audit. Resolved by per-target
  source/state citations and separate source-reviewed, runtime-exercised and owner-accepted status.
- Future archaeologist: numerical averages could be mistaken for measured mouse behavior. Resolved
  by preserving origin assumptions, model choice, units and evidence gaps in each component record.
- Scope sniper: an audit could turn into an unattended redesign or a tooling rewrite. Resolved by
  excluding component repairs and limiting tooling work to independently specified blockers.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Scope includes all 52 exported types, not only the 31-type production subset. Initial plan is apply-ready and awaits the owner gate before audit execution. Per-element contracts and findings extend docs/components/<Type>.md, shared method/index use docs/USAGE.md. Hitbox math uses actual input geometry, stated origins/approach width, ID in bits, clearance and corridor timing. It never claims average human movement or milliseconds from uncalibrated synthetic paths. Runtime session capture is separately specified as br-g9t in qsm-workbench.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Audit runtime evidence path is now available. The Workbench capture change (qsm-workbench br-g9t) is implemented, verified 7/7, and installed to the local prefix. It captures the CURRENT state of an explicitly selected session, preview scope or window scope, preserves held presses and provider state, and refuses to overwrite an output. A glyph component such as IconButton is transparent offscreen in both scopes, because the offscreen pipeline does not rasterise SvgIcon glyphs (qsm-shell AGENTS.md). Visual evidence for glyph-bearing types therefore needs a real window on workspace 10, while geometry, tree, input and state evidence works headless. The audit can now start: 52 exported types, 60 story keys, one coverage row per type in docs/USAGE.md, per-type records in docs/components/<Type>.md with hitbox and pointer-path mathematics.

title: Decide the shared design direction and the first repair item
description:
Why: the audit (qss-9zk.2) produces findings and a proposed design direction, but the owner decides which component is repaired first and what the shared visual direction becomes. The owner explicitly allowed a full redesign including the shared silhouette, so the old project rules (no shadow, no separate chrome, the surface ladder) are candidates for revision, not defences against a finding.

What this task settles, in one owner session:
1. Which shared rules change: the surface ladder and its steps, the ban on shadows and borders, the silhouette itself, the palette roles, the spacing and type scales, the motion vocabulary. Each decision is recorded in the design source the audits read, with the reason and the owner's words.
2. Which type is repaired first, and what done looks like for it.
3. Whether the repair order follows the desktop's own priority or the audit's severity.

How: the owner reviews the delivered audit (qss-9zk.2), the design conflicts it filed, and the proposed candidates. The agent writes the decisions into the design source and the affected specs in the same move, citing the owner, then creates one spec change and one tracker task per selected repair item. Every repair item gets its own spec and its own owner acceptance before the next one starts.

Done when: the shared design decisions are written in the owning document, the first repair item has its spec and task, and the desktop task in ../qsm-desktop is still blocked on the library.

Not in this task: repairing the components themselves, the desktop, and the audit's remaining records.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Dependency direction: qss-9zk.2 (the audit) blocks this task, and this task blocks qss-9zk.1 (the owner trial). The chain is audit, then owner decision on the shared direction and the first repair, then the trial. Claimed for the next session so the ready list shows it.

title: Menu and MonthCalendar can replace bindings owned by their host
description: Found during the workspace ownership audit. Menu.qml:95,107,143 writes selection directly despite host-owned selection wording. MonthCalendar.qml:17 assigns shown before monthShifted(), while its component record calls the month host-owned. These source-confirmed local ownership mismatches can replace QML bindings; they are not singleton fullscreen leaks. Acceptance: each type reports intent through its shared public action and lets the host update the bound state. Runtime binding behavior and owner review remain unverified. Repair one type at a time under its component record.

title: NotificationCard: entry.actions from the bus is a QVariantList, .find/.some throw
description: Seen 2026-10-17 on the live desktop after one protocol notification: NotificationCard.qml:180 defaultAction() calls (root.entry.actions ?? []).find and NotificationStack.qml:407 calls .some on payload.actions; the actions value arriving from the desktop's NotificationEntry.presentationRecord is a V4ReferenceObject (a QVariantList reference), which has no Array methods, so both warn 'Property find of object [object V4ReferenceObject] is not a function' and the default action is never found. Fix in the library: copy with Array.from (or Array.prototype.slice.call) before .find/.some, in one shared helper; the consumer must not have to pre-copy.

title: README: add images of the component catalog
description: what: the public README has no visuals of the components, tokens or the edge shader. how: capture a few representative components (button, text field, notification card, panel with the edge shader) through qsm-workbench with the qsm-shell provider (flow-runner --window --capture, or grim on a workbench window), assemble one overview image, store under docs/assets/, link in README. why: a component library is judged by how it looks; without images a reviewer has nothing to look at. needs: a live Wayland session with wf-recorder; workbench capture is user-driven by design.
